about: Johnnie Walker is the world's best-selling Scotch whisky brand, owned by Diageo and tied to Kilmarnock, East Ayrshire, in Scotland, where it was founded in 1820. Its range includes Red Label, Black Label, Double Black, Green Label, Gold Label Reserve and Blue Label, sold in around 180 countries. Diageo is listed in London. Johnnie Walker has a long record of motorsport and F1 sponsorship, so it is a natural fit for the sport and a likely existing partner.

Drinks manufacturer, marketer and distributor with a portfolio of cider and beer brands including Bulmers (in Ireland), Magners, Tennent's lager and Menabrea, plus an on-trade distribution arm serving pubs, restaurants and hotels across the UK and Ireland. Revenue comes from alcohol sales and wholesale distribution, with annual sales well over one billion euros. Headquartered in Glasgow with roots in Ireland, it is listed in Dublin and London (CCR). Customers are pubs, retailers and consumers; brand visibility is high in Britain and Ireland, with a long history of sport and festival sponsorship.

Chinese wine and spirits company based in Urumqi in Xinjiang, with Crunchbase tagging in sales and wine and spirits and a listed status in the data. Xinjiang is a wine-growing region, so it likely produces or trades wine, but the exact brands, vineyards, customers and sales channels cannot be confirmed from the available information. Scale and ownership are not clear. It is a regional name with no confirmed national consumer profile, so details should be verified from the website or filings before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

North American beverage company formed in 2018, combining Keurig Green Mountain coffee brewers and K-Cups with Dr Pepper Snapple's soft drinks, including Dr Pepper, 7UP, Canada Dry, Snapple, A&W and Core, and the acquisition of GHOST energy drinks. Sells to consumers through retailers and foodservice, with revenue near 15 billion dollars. Headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts and Frisco, Texas. Listed on Nasdaq (KDP), with JAB Holding a major holder; it announced a 2025 plan to acquire JDE Peet's. Strong US consumer brands.

French hospitality group operating or franchising about 5,700 hotels in 110 countries under brands such as Sofitel, Pullman, Novotel, Mercure, Ibis, Fairmont, Raffles, Swissotel, Mövenpick and the Ennismore lifestyle brands, plus ALL loyalty and sport venue naming. Earns management and franchise fees. Headquartered in Issy-les-Moulineaux near Paris. Listed on Euronext Paris (AC), with Saudi PIF-linked Kingdom Holding a significant shareholder. Established consumer brands and an experienced sports sponsor, including Paris venue and football partnerships.

Second-largest US grocery chain, operating about 2,200 stores with 1,700 pharmacies under banners including Safeway, Albertsons, Vons, Jewel-Osco, Shaw's and Acme, plus the Signature Select private-label range. Customers are everyday shoppers, and it earns grocery, pharmacy and fuel revenue of near 80 billion dollars. Headquartered in Boise, Idaho; roughly 280,000 employees. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ACI). Its planned merger with Kroger was blocked in December 2024. Well-known US supermarket banners.

Canadian convenience store and fuel retailer operating Circle K, Couche-Tard and Ingo, with around 17,000 stores in 29 countries across North America, Europe and Asia. Sells fuel, fast food and everyday items to consumers, with revenue near 70 billion dollars. Headquartered in Laval, Quebec; founded 1980. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ATD). It pursued a 2025 bid for Seven & i, which later was withdrawn. Circle K is a very recognisable consumer brand and a past motorsport sponsor.

Switzerland-based world's largest chocolate and cocoa product maker, supplying industrial and artisan chocolatiers, bakeries, food manufacturers and restaurants with chocolate, cocoa and fillings under Callebaut, Cacao Barry and Van Houten. Revenue near 8 billion Swiss francs and about 13,000 employees in over 30 countries. Headquartered in Zurich; formed in 1996. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (BARN), with Jacobs Holding and Renata Coray related interests. B2B ingredient supplier with limited consumer brand awareness, though its brands are professional favourites.

US food company known for Greek yogurt, also selling oat milk, creamers, coffee drinks, kefir and probiotics. Founded in 2005 by Hamdi Ulukaya, with its largest facilities in New Berlin, New York and Twin Falls, Idaho, and revenue near 3 billion dollars plus. Sells through supermarkets across the US and abroad. Privately held, with TPG and others as investors; raised large capital in 2025 at a valuation of 20 billion dollars. Strong consumer brand and a sponsor of US Olympic and Paralympic teams.

French food and beverage group making dairy and plant-based products, specialised nutrition and water, with brands like Activia, Actimel, Alpro, Danonino, Evian, Volvic, Oikos, Silk and baby formula brands Aptamil and Nutricia. Sells to consumers through retail worldwide in more than 120 markets, with revenue near 27 billion euros and about 90,000 employees. Headquartered in Paris; founded 1919. Listed on Euronext Paris (BN). Very strong consumer brands and a regular sports sponsor (Evian and Volvic in sport).

US quick-service restaurant chain with about 2,200 Jack in the Box locations in several states, mostly California and Texas, known for tacos, burgers and late-night menus, and it owned Del Taco, acquired in 2022. Sells to consumers through franchisees, with revenue near 1.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in San Diego, California; founded 1951. Listed on Nasdaq (JACK). Del Taco divestiture was announced in 2025. Regional fast-food brand with strong awareness in the West and South.

World's largest meat company, processing beef, pork, chicken and lamb and selling under Seara, Swift, Friboi, Pilgrim's Pride, Moy Park and Primo Foods brands as well as plant-based Vivera. Customers are retailers, food service and consumers in over 190 countries, with revenue near 70 to 80 billion dollars. Headquartered in Sao Paulo, Brazil; founded 1953 by the Batista family, who control it. It listed on the New York Stock Exchange (JBS) in 2025, with a Brazilian listing too. Mostly B2B, with consumer brands in some markets, and a past sponsor of football and sports.

Europe's largest frozen food company owning Birds Eye, Findus and iglo, selling frozen fish, vegetables, poultry, ready meals and pizza to consumers through supermarkets in the UK, Italy, Germany, France, Sweden and elsewhere, with revenue near 3.3 billion euros. Headquartered in Woking, Surrey; formed in 2014 and previously known as Iglo Group. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NOMD) and has the London Stock Exchange listing. Familiar consumer brands, especially Birds Eye in the UK.

Olam Food Ingredients is the food and beverage ingredients business of Olam Group, supplying cocoa, coffee, dairy, nuts and spices to food manufacturers and retailers. Customers are food and beverage producers worldwide, with the coffee and cocoa lines among the largest globally. Headquartered in Singapore; Olam Group is majority owned by Singapore's Temasek. ofi was set up in 2022 as a separate business within Olam and has been preparing for a separate listing. B2B ingredient supplier with limited consumer awareness.

about: One of the world's largest chicken producers, with processing plants in the United States, Mexico, the UK and Europe, making fresh and prepared chicken and pork sold to retailers and food service customers, and under brands such as Pilgrim's, Just Bare and Moy Park. Revenue near 17 billion dollars. Headquartered in Greeley, Colorado; founded 1946. Listed on Nasdaq (PPC) and majority controlled by JBS. A familiar food brand in the US supermarket aisle, with sponsorship through events such as NASCAR.

Consumer packaged goods holding company with brands in cereal (Post Consumer Brands, Honey Bunches of Oats, Pebbles, Malt-O-Meal), refrigerated foods (Michael Foods, Bob Evans), foodservice and pet food (Nutrish and Nutro acquired from Smucker's) and more. Customers include grocery stores, restaurants and consumers across North America and Europe, with revenue near 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in St Louis, Missouri; spun out of Ralcorp in 2012. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (POST). Well-known US cereal brands.

Wonder is a US food and mealtime company that operates food halls, restaurant brands and meal delivery from Wonder, led by founder Marc Lore, and acquired Grubhub in 2025. Offers multi-restaurant ordering with chef-driven concepts via trucks and mobile kitchens in the New Jersey and New York region. Funding in the input is around 3.2 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York. Growing but emerging consumer brand in the US Northeast, with a lot of media attention.

about: Southeast Asia's leading super app, offering ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery (GrabFood), digital payments and financial services (GrabPay), across eight countries including Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia and Vietnam. Earns commissions, advertising and financial fees, with about 40 million monthly users. Headquartered in Singapore; founded 2012 in Malaysia. Listed on Nasdaq (GRAB) since its 2021 SPAC merger. Strong consumer brand across Southeast Asia and a Formula 1 sponsor (Grab as a title sponsor of the Singapore Grand Prix).

World's largest temperature-controlled warehousing and logistics provider, with over 400 cold storage facilities across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, storing and transporting food for retailers, producers and distributors. Revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Novi, Michigan; founded 2008. Listed on Nasdaq (LINE) after a record 2024 IPO of about 4.4 billion dollars, with Bay Grove Capital and others as shareholders. B2B logistics brand with essentially no consumer awareness.

British premium spirits and beer company owning Johnnie Walker, Smirnoff, Guinness, Tanqueray, Don Julio, Captain Morgan, Baileys and Crown Royal, sold in about 180 countries with revenue near 20 billion dollars. Customers are consumers via retailers, bars and restaurants and e-commerce. Headquartered in London; formed in 1997 from Guinness and Grand Metropolitan. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (DGE) and New York (DEO). Very strong consumer brands and a major sports sponsor, including Formula 1 as an official global Formula 1 partner through Johnnie Walker and Guinness 0.0.

One of the world's largest ice cream makers, producing brands under licence and in-house including Nestle brands under licence such as Drumstick and Maxibon, plus its own Mini Milk, Oreo and Cadbury ice cream licences and Cornetto-type novelties. Formed in 2016 as a joint venture of Nestle and PAI Partners. Sells to consumers through retailers in more than 20 countries, with revenue near 4 billion euros. Headquartered in Harrogate, North Yorkshire. Privately held. Corporate name little known; consumers know the product brands.

about: French wine and spirits group owning Absolut, Jameson, Chivas Regal, Ballantine's, Martell, Havana Club, The Glenlivet, Beefeater, Malibu, Kahlua and Perrier-Jouet, sold in over 160 countries. Revenue near 11 billion euros and about 19,000 employees. Headquartered in Paris; formed in 1975 from Pernod and Ricard, with the Ricard family a large shareholder. Listed on Euronext Paris (RI). Very strong consumer brands and an active sponsor of sports and music.

The Magnum Ice Cream Company was demerged from Unilever in December 2025, owning Magnum, Wall's, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto, Algida, Klondike, Breyers and Talenti, selling frozen desserts to consumers through retailers and freezers in about 100 countries. Revenue near 8 billion euros. Headquartered in Amsterdam. Listed in Amsterdam, London and New York. Very strong consumer ice cream brands.

about: US restaurant franchise operator with KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and The Habit Burger & Grill, with over 60,000 restaurants in more than 155 countries and a heavily franchised model that earns royalties. Revenue near 7.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky; spun off from PepsiCo in 1997. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (YUM). Separate Yum China is a listed entity. Very strong consumer fast-food brands and long-standing sports sponsors, including Taco Bell's links with motorsport.

Grupo Nutresa is a Colombian processed food group making cold cuts, chocolates, biscuits, coffee, ice cream (Helados Crem Helado) and pasta, with brands such as Colcafe, Noel, Zenu and Jet. Customers are consumers across Latin America, with revenue near 3 billion dollars. Headquartered in Medellin. Controlled since 2025 by the Gilinski family's Nugil, which took control from Grupo Sura and Argos in a takeover. Trades on the Colombian Stock Exchange (NUTRESA). Strong Colombian consumer brands.

Constellation Brands is a US beverage alcohol company best known for imported Mexican beers (Corona, Modelo, Pacifico) which it brews for the US market, plus wine and spirits such as Robert Mondavi, Meiomi and Casa Noble (Kim Crawford sold in 2024). Revenue near 10 billion dollars. Headquartered in Victor, New York (input shows Rochester). Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (STZ). Very strong beer brands and a long-time sponsor of sports including UFC, boxing and motorsport.

Guala Closures is an Italian maker of aluminium and plastic closures for spirits, wine, water, beverage and oil bottles, including tamper-evident and anti-counterfeiting designs. Customers are global drinks groups. Operates plants in about 30 countries. Headquartered in Spinetta Marengo, Piedmont; founded 1954. Taken private by Investindustrial in 2018 after its 2007 listing. B2B packaging supplier with no consumer awareness.

McCormick & Company is a US spice, seasoning and flavour company, owning McCormick, Frank's RedHot, French's, Cholula, Old Bay, Lawry's, Schwartz, Club House and Ducros, plus flavour solutions sold to food manufacturers and restaurants. Revenue near 6.7 billion dollars. Headquartered in Hunt Valley, Maryland (Sparks); founded 1889. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (MKC). Strong consumer pantry brands, with some sports partnerships.

Mondelez International is a global snacking group, with Oreo, Cadbury, Milka, Toblerone, Ritz, Chips Ahoy, Trident, Halls and Sour Patch Kids, sold in more than 150 countries. Revenue near 38 billion dollars and about 90,000 employees. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois; spun off from Kraft Foods in 2012. Listed on Nasdaq (MDLZ). Very strong consumer brands and an active sports and events sponsor, including Olympic and football partnerships.

Performance Food Group is a US foodservice distributor delivering food and supplies to restaurants, schools, hospitals and convenience stores through Performance Foodservice, Vistar and Core-Mark (acquired 2021). Revenue near 60 billion dollars. Headquartered in Richmond, Virginia; founded 1885. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (PFGC). B2B distributor, little consumer awareness.

Tyson Foods is one of the largest US protein producers, processing chicken, beef and pork and selling prepared foods under Tyson, Jimmy Dean, Hillshire Farm, Ball Park and Sara Lee. Customers are retailers, restaurants and consumers, with revenue near 53 billion dollars and about 140,000 employees. Headquartered in Springdale, Arkansas; founded 1935 by John Tyson. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TSN). Very recognisable US food brand and long-time NASCAR and sports sponsor.

Subway is one of the world's largest restaurant franchises, with about 37,000 locations in over 100 countries, selling made-to-order sandwiches, salads and wraps. Based in Milford, Connecticut, though Crunchbase lists a Canadian address. Operations are overwhelmingly franchised, earning royalties and fees from franchisees. In 2024 it was acquired by Roark Capital for about $9.6bn, taking over from founders' families. Private. Extremely high global consumer brand awareness and a regular sports sponsor and advertiser.

Zomato (now Eternal Ltd) is a Gurugram-based Indian online food delivery and restaurant discovery platform, also operating the quick-commerce service Blinkit, going-out dining service District, and B2B supplier Hyperpure. It earns commissions, delivery and advertising fees from tens of millions of customers and hundreds of thousands of restaurants in India. It listed in Mumbai (NSE/BSE) in 2021 and renamed the group Eternal in 2025. Very strong consumer brand across India, a visible advertiser and cricket sponsor.

AWL Agri Business (formerly Adani Wilmar) is an Ahmedabad-based Indian FMCG and agri company, best known for Fortune cooking oils, plus rice, wheat flour, pulses, sugar and soaps. It sells packaged staples to Indian households and bulk oils and oleochemicals to industry, with annual revenue around INR 600bn. It was a joint venture of Adani Group and Wilmar International; Adani sold its stake to Wilmar in 2025, and the company was renamed AWL. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Fortune is a major consumer brand in India with heavy advertising.

Carrefour is a French multinational retail group, based in Massy, running hypermarkets, supermarkets, convenience stores, cash-and-carry and e-commerce in France, Spain, Italy, Belgium, Brazil, Argentina and other countries, with about 14,000 stores, 300,000+ staff and revenue of roughly EUR 90bn. It earns from grocery and non-food sales, plus banking, insurance and retail media. Listed on Euronext Paris (CA); the Moulin family via Galfa and Peninsula Europe are key shareholders. Very strong consumer brand, a long-time sponsor of sport such as the Tour de France and French football.

McDonald's is the world's largest restaurant chain by revenue, based in Chicago, with about 43,000 locations in over 100 countries selling burgers, fries, chicken and breakfast items. About 95 percent of restaurants are franchised, so it earns rent and royalties from franchisees plus sales at company-run units. Annual revenue is about $26bn and market capitalisation is above $200bn. Listed on the NYSE (MCD). Among the best-known consumer brands in the world and a veteran global sponsor (Olympics, FIFA World Cup, UEFA), with strong F1 relevance for family audiences.

Bloomin' Brands is a Tampa, Florida restaurant group operating Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse, with about 1,450 restaurants in the US, Brazil and other international markets, including franchises. Revenue is about $4bn. Listed on Nasdaq (BLMN). Strong casual dining consumer brands, especially Outback in the US and Brazil, and a regular sports sponsor and advertiser.

Flink is a Berlin-based quick-commerce grocery delivery company, delivering groceries in minutes from dark stores in Germany, the Netherlands and Austria. It earns product margins and delivery fees from urban consumers, and has raised about $1.5bn including a 2022 round led by REWE and Mubadala at a $2.1bn valuation. REWE Group is its largest shareholder. Private. Consumer brand with solid awareness in German cities, though with modest advertising budgets.

Hindustan Urvarak and Rasayan Limited (HURL) is a New Delhi-based fertilizer maker formed as a joint venture of NTPC, Coal India, Indian Oil and the Fertilizer Corporation of India and Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation to revive urea plants at Gorakhpur, Sindri and Barauni. Customers are Indian farmers supplied through government distribution, funded by central subsidies. State-linked and privately held, with funding shown at INR 128bn. B2B and government-linked, with no consumer brand.

MBRF is the Brazilian food group formed in 2025 by the merger of Marfrig and BRF, headquartered in Sao Paulo. Its brands include Sadia, Perdigao, Qualy, Bassi and Marfrig, covering beef, chicken, pork, processed and plant-based foods, selling in Brazil and over 140 countries, with revenue above BRL 150bn and a workforce of about 150,000. Listed on B3 (MBRF3). Strong consumer brands in Brazil, and Sadia and Perdigao have a long history of football sponsorship.

Global Eggs is a privately owned holding group from Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil, that operates in egg production and egg products for the consumer goods and food industry, according to Crunchbase. The input shows funding of about $1bn with the latest round in March 2026. No further detail on brands, scale or ownership is given. Food manufacturing supplier. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Bunge is a St. Louis-area (Chesterfield, Missouri) global agribusiness and food ingredient company that buys, stores, processes and trades oilseeds and grains such as soybeans, corn and wheat, and sells vegetable oils, flour, meal and sugar. In 2025 it completed its purchase of Viterra. Customers are food producers, feed makers and biofuel firms worldwide, and revenue is about $50-60bn. Listed on the NYSE (BG). B2B commodity group with low consumer awareness.

Molson Coors is a Chicago-based global brewer, with brands Coors Light, Miller Lite, Molson Canadian, Blue Moon, Carling, Staropramen and Madri, selling in the US, Canada, Europe and other markets, with revenue near $11bn and about 16,000 employees. It also has a growing non-beer beverage portfolio. Listed on the NYSE (TAP). Very strong consumer brands, and a heavy long-running sports sponsor, including NHL, NFL and soccer.

COFCO Fortune is the food brand and edible oil business of China's state-owned COFCO Group, operating from Beijing and selling Fortune-branded cooking oil, rice, flour, noodles and other packaged foods to Chinese households. Funding of about CNY 21bn came in a 2023 round. State-linked. A major packaged-food consumer brand in China, with extensive retail presence and advertising, little known abroad.

General Mills is a Minneapolis-based global packaged food company with brands such as Cheerios, Nature Valley, Haagen-Dazs, Pillsbury, Betty Crocker, Yoplait, Old El Paso, Blue Buffalo pet food and Annie's. It sells through grocery and foodservice channels in more than 100 countries, with revenue near $19bn and about 34,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (GIS). Highly recognised consumer brands in North America and abroad, with large advertising budgets and sports sponsorships.

Avril Group is a Paris-based French agro-industrial and financial group, created by French farmers' organisations, owning edible oil and biofuel producer Saipol, Lesieur and Puget (consumer oil brands), Sofiproteol, Diester and animal nutrition business Sanders. Revenue is near EUR 9-10bn. It is a cooperative-style group, not listed. Several household food brands in France, with the Lesieur oil brand widely recognised, otherwise B2B.

Domino's Pizza is an Ann Arbor, Michigan pizza chain with over 21,000 stores in more than 90 countries, mostly franchised, including delivery and carry-out, with strong digital ordering. System-wide sales are above $19bn. Master franchisees such as Domino's Pizza Enterprises (Australia) and DP Eurasia operate abroad. Listed on the NYSE (DPZ). Very high consumer brand awareness, with big advertising spend and sports sponsorships, such as NASCAR and MLS.

Haldiram's Snacks is the Noida, Uttar Pradesh-based Indian snack food company behind Haldiram's bhujia, namkeen, sweets, ready-to-eat meals and packaged foods, sold through retail in India and exported to dozens of countries. It is a family-founded group with Bikaner, Nagpur and Delhi entities. In 2025 Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Alpha Wave and Temasek bought minority stakes valuing it at around $10bn. Private. Beloved Indian consumer brand with big advertising reach.

J.B. Poindexter and Co. is a Houston, Texas privately held diversified manufacturer, owning businesses that produce truck bodies (Morgan Truck Body, Morgan Olson), pickup truck accessories (Truck Accessories Group, including Leer), specialty vehicles, and EFP/Reading Truck Body-style components. Customers are fleet operators, delivery firms and consumers. Controlled by chairman John Poindexter, with revenue around $1.5bn. Private. B2B brand known in fleet and truck circles, not to the public.

Premium Brands Holdings is a Richmond, British Columbia food manufacturer and distributor, producing specialty foods such as sandwiches, deli meats, Italian meats, protein and snacks, and distributing wholesale food products across Canada and the western US. Revenue is around C$6.5bn. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (PBH). Largely B2B (grocery and foodservice supply), with some private-label work, so consumer brand awareness is low.

Del Monte Foods is a Walnut Creek, California US maker of canned fruit, vegetables and tomatoes under Del Monte, Contadina, S&W and College Inn, sold in supermarkets nationwide, with ownership by Del Monte Pacific (Philippines). It filed for Chapter 11 in July 2025 and sold most assets to buyers, including Fresh Del Monte-style and private-equity buyers. Funding shown is about $912m, reflecting financing. Well-known US grocery brand, though now restructured and parted out.

Dine Brands Global is a Pasadena, California restaurant franchisor, owning Applebee's Neighborhood Grill + Bar, IHOP and Fuzzy's Taco Shop, with about 3,500 restaurants in the US and abroad, nearly all franchised. It earns royalties and franchise fees, with revenue near $0.9bn. Listed on the NYSE (DIN). Applebee's and IHOP are very recognisable casual dining brands in the US, with strong advertising and sports and entertainment tie-ins.

Quirch Foods is a Coral Gables, Florida food distributor and exporter of beef, pork, poultry and seafood, supplying supermarkets, foodservice and processors across Latin America, the Caribbean and the US from US and international suppliers. It was created by Quirch family and was combined with Sysco-related businesses. Privately held. B2B protein supplier with little consumer awareness.

Hershey is a Pennsylvania-based confectionery and snack company founded in 1894, making Hershey's chocolate, Reese's, Kisses, Kit Kat (US license), Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, plus salty snacks such as SkinnyPop and Dot's Pretzels. Customers are consumers via grocery, mass retailers and convenience stores, mainly in North America, with sales of about $11 billion. Listed on NYSE (HSY), controlled by the Hershey Trust. Household-name consumer brand with heavy marketing.

JDE Peet's is an Amsterdam-based global coffee and tea company, created by the 2020 merger of Jacobs Douwe Egberts and Peet's Coffee. Brands include Douwe Egberts, Jacobs, L'OR, Tassimo, Senseo, Peet's and Pickwick, sold in more than 100 markets with revenue of roughly 9 billion euros. Customers are consumers via retailers and foodservice. Controlled by JAB Holding and listed on Euronext Amsterdam from 2020; Keurig Dr Pepper agreed to acquire it in 2025. Well-known grocery brands in Europe.

Equity Invest is a US investment company, listed in food and beverage and healthcare industries, offering strategic investments. The input reports funding of about $846 million, but gives no specifics on holdings or owners. No further reliable detail is available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Jersey Mike's Subs is a Manasquan, New Jersey sub sandwich franchisor founded in 1956, with about 3,000 restaurants in the US, and sales of over $3 billion. Customers are consumers buying sandwiches in-store and online. Blackstone acquired it in 2024 in a deal valuing it at about $8 billion; the input shows reported funding of $760 million. Strong US consumer brand, a sponsor of sports including NASCAR and the Jersey Mike's 400.

Sucro Sourcing is a US food ingredient processing company that offers sugar and sweetener sourcing, refining and supply, and in recent years has focused on sugar refining operations in the Southeastern US. The input shows reported funding of about $839 million. Customers are food and beverage manufacturers. B2B ingredients supplier with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Vilmorin & Cie is the French vegetable and field seed company (Limagrain's listed subsidiary), now called Limagrain's seed arm, headquartered in Clermont-Ferrand. It breeds, produces and markets vegetable and field crop seeds through brands such as Vilmorin-Mikado, Hazera, Vilmorin Garden, and others, selling in over 150 countries. Majority-owned by the Limagrain cooperative, and delisted from Euronext Paris after a 2024 buyout. B2B agriculture, with some consumer garden brands.

about: Coca-Cola FEMSA is a Mexico City-based beverage company, the world's largest franchise bottler of Coca-Cola products, serving Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Argentina and other Latin American countries, with over 250 million consumers and 3.9 billion unit cases sold. Owned partly by FEMSA and The Coca-Cola Company, it is listed on the Mexican exchange (KOF UBL) and NYSE (KOF). Customers are retailers, restaurants and consumers. Strong visibility via Coca-Cola brands, including sponsorship activity.

Eroski is a Basque-country Spanish retail cooperative group based in Elorrio, Bizkaia, running supermarkets, hypermarkets, fuel stations and travel and online stores, such as Eroski, Caprabo and Vegalsa-Eroski, with over 1,500 outlets. Owned by workers and consumers as a cooperative, with about 540 million euros in reported funding. Customers are shoppers in Spain. Well-known grocery brand in northern Spain.

B&G Foods is a Parsippany, New Jersey packaged-food company with a portfolio of shelf-stable and frozen brands including Green Giant, Crisco, Ortega, Cream of Wheat, Maple Grove Farms and Clabber Girl, sold through grocery and foodservice channels in North America. Revenue is around $2 billion. Listed on NYSE (BGS). Customers are grocery retailers and consumers. Several household brands, though the corporate name is little known.

Luckin Coffee is a Xiamen, China-based coffee chain, founded in 2017, with more than 24,000 stores in China, selling coffee, tea and snacks mostly through a mobile app for pickup and delivery. It overtook Starbucks in China store count. After a 2020 accounting fraud scandal it was delisted from Nasdaq, restructured and traded over the counter, and is controlled by Centurium Capital. Very high consumer brand awareness in China, with global expansion into Singapore and the US starting.

O-I Glass is a Perrysburg, Ohio-based glass container manufacturer, one of the world's largest, producing bottles and jars for beer, wine, spirits, food and beverage brands from more than 70 plants in about 19 countries. Revenue is around $6.5 billion. Listed on NYSE (OI). Customers are brewers, distillers and food makers, not consumers. B2B packaging supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Maple Leaf Foods is a Canadian packaged meats and plant-based protein company headquartered in Mississauga, Ontario, listed on the TSX (MFI). Brands include Maple Leaf, Schneiders, Schneiders Country Naturals, Greenfield Natural Meat, Lightlife and Field Roast, sold through grocers and foodservice in Canada, the US and Asia, with about 14,000 employees and revenue near 4.9 billion Canadian dollars. It is controlled by McCain family interests. Established in 1927 as Canada Packers. Strong Canadian consumer brand with sports sponsorship history.

Roquette America is the US arm of Roquette, the French family-owned plant-based ingredients group founded in 1933 in Lestrem. It makes starch, sweeteners, proteins such as pea protein, and excipients for food, nutrition and pharmaceutical customers worldwide, with about 10,000 employees and revenue near 4 billion euros. The input lists a French location. Customers are food and drug manufacturers. B2B ingredient supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB) is the Indian bottling and distribution arm of the Coca-Cola system, headquartered in Gurugram with a base shown in Bengaluru, producing and selling Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, Thums Up, Limca, Maaza and Minute Maid across India through plants and millions of retail outlets. It is owned by The Coca-Cola Company, which agreed in 2025 to sell a stake of about 40 percent to the Jubilant Bhartia group. Mass consumer reach and an active sponsor of cricket and events in India.

Oatly is a Swedish oat-drink company headquartered in Malmo and listed on Nasdaq (OTLY), selling oat milk, ice cream, spreads and cooking products in about 20 markets through supermarkets and coffee shops. Founded in the 1990s from Lund University research, its backers have included Blackstone, Verlinvest, Oprah Winfrey and China Resources, which was the major shareholder. Revenue is around 800 million dollars. Strong lifestyle consumer brand with distinctive advertising.

Fruitist is a Los Angeles-based food and beverage company that, according to its Crunchbase profile, designs, grows and distributes premium fruit. Customers are likely retailers and consumers buying branded fresh fruit, but products, scale, ownership and funding details are not confirmed from the input. Consumer-facing food brand with unknown awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Rebel Foods is an Indian cloud kitchen and food-tech company headquartered in Mumbai that runs multiple delivery-only restaurant brands including Faasos, Behrouz Biryani, Oven Story Pizza, Lunch Box and Sweet Truth from hundreds of kitchens, ordering through Zomato, Swiggy and its own app. Founded 2011 as Faasos. It has raised funding from Goldman Sachs, Coatue and Qatar Investment Authority at a valuation above 1.4 billion dollars. Strong consumer food delivery brands in India.

Dmall is a Beijing-based retail technology company describing itself as Asia's leading retail cloud solution provider, offering omnichannel retail software, order fulfilment and delivery platforms for supermarkets and retailers in China and Southeast Asia, including clients such as Metro and Wumart. Founded 2015, formerly part of Wumart's e-commerce arm, backed by Tencent, Alibaba-linked and other investors. Customers are retail chains. B2B technology with limited public awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Grupo Uvesco is a Spanish food retail and consumer goods group based in Irun in the Basque Country, operating supermarkets and wholesale distribution in northern Spain under banners such as BM Supermercados and Super Amara. It also runs logistics and local product sourcing. Customers are Spanish shoppers, and revenue comes from food retail. Established regional brand with limited recognition elsewhere. about: Tate & Lyle is a British specialty food and beverage ingredients company headquartered in London and listed on the LSE (TATE). It makes sweeteners such as sucralose, soluble fibres, texturants and stabilisers for food, drink and health products, selling to multinational manufacturers. Revenue is about 2 billion pounds. Founded 1921 through a merger of sugar refiners. Sold its controlling stake in the Primient corn business in 2024. B2B ingredients supplier with low consumer awareness.

Tesco is the UK's largest supermarket group, headquartered in Welwyn Garden City, Hertfordshire and listed on the LSE (TSCO). It operates thousands of Tesco, Express and Extra stores plus Booker wholesale, Clubcard loyalty and Tesco Bank (now largely sold), with operations in Ireland and Central Europe, 330,000 employees and revenue over 68 billion pounds. Founded 1919. Customers are mainstream shoppers. Hugely recognisable consumer brand with prior sponsorships in sport and charity.

Starbucks is the world's largest coffee chain, headquartered in Seattle, Washington and listed on Nasdaq (SBUX). It operates about 40,000 company-owned and licensed stores in over 80 countries, selling coffee, tea, food and packaged goods, with about 380,000 employees and revenue near 36 billion dollars. Founded 1971. Customers are mainstream consumers; also earns from Nestle licensing of packaged products. One of the most recognised consumer brands globally with loyalty programme and heavy marketing.

Scandi Standard is a Nordic poultry producer headquartered in Stockholm and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (SCST), producing chicken for supermarkets and foodservice under brands such as Kronfagel (Sweden), Danpo (Denmark), Den Stolte Hane (Norway) and Naapurin Maalaiskana (Finland), with revenue about 15 billion Swedish kronor. Founded 2010 as a roll-up of local producers. Customers are grocers and restaurants. Recognised grocery brand in the Nordics with a regional consumer profile.

Cal-Maine Foods is the largest producer and distributor of fresh shell eggs in the United States, selling conventional, cage-free, organic and specialty eggs under brands such as Egg-Land's Best, Land O'Lakes and Farmhouse Eggs, plus egg products. Customers are grocery chains, foodservice distributors and food manufacturers. Based in Ridgeland, Mississippi, with over 50 million laying hens. Listed on Nasdaq (CALM), with revenue well above $2 billion in strong egg price years. Moderate consumer brand awareness; largely a commodity supplier.

Clearwater Paper produces private-label tissue (bath tissue, paper towels, facial tissue and napkins) for US retailers, plus paperboard for folding cartons and food service. Customers are grocery, club and discount retailers, who sell the products under their own store brands, and packaging converters. Headquartered in Spokane, Washington, it spun out from Potlatch in 2008. Revenue is about $1.4 to 1.6 billion. Listed on NYSE (CLW). B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Co-operative Group is a UK consumer co-operative owned by around 2.5 million members, running Co-op Food convenience and grocery stores, Co-op Funeralcare, Co-op Legal Services and Co-op Insurance. Based in Manchester, with about 2,300 food stores and annual revenue over 11 billion pounds. Customers are UK consumers, who earn member rewards. Mutually owned and not listed. Well-known UK consumer brand with a strong community presence.

Ecom Agroindustrial, now ECOM Trading, is a global commodity merchant specialising in coffee, cocoa and cotton, buying from farmers in producing countries and supplying roasters, chocolate makers and textile mills. Based in Pully, Switzerland, with operations in over 40 countries and revenue in the order of $10 billion or more. Privately held, not listed. Revenue from trading, processing and logistics. B2B, with little public brand awareness.

COFCO International is the agricultural trading and processing arm of China's state-owned COFCO Group, buying, storing, processing and shipping grains, oilseeds, sugar, coffee, cotton and other commodities worldwide. Headquartered in Geneva (Chene-Bougeries), Switzerland, and active in the Americas, Europe, the Black Sea and Asia. Customers are food and feed manufacturers and importers. Revenue is in the tens of billions of dollars. State-owned through COFCO. B2B, with limited consumer brand awareness.

Westrock Coffee is a Little Rock, Arkansas company that sources, roasts and processes coffee, tea and extracts, produces ready-to-drink beverages and sells through its Westrock Coffee, with a large Conway, Arkansas extract and RTD facility. Customers are restaurant chains, retailers and consumer brands, and it also sells under private label, with revenue of about $900 million. Listed on Nasdaq (WEST). Mostly B2B, with limited consumer brand awareness.

MIDERA Food Processing is a manufacturer of industrial food processing equipment, according to Crunchbase, and is based in Elk Grove Village, Illinois. It is classified under food processing and industrial. Crunchbase shows about $1 billion in funding, which looks large and may reflect a group financing or a data quirk. Products, customers and ownership are not stated in the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Papa John's is a US pizza delivery and carryout chain with about 6,000 restaurants in nearly 50 countries, mostly franchised, selling pizza, sides and desserts, with online ordering as a main channel. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia (moved from Louisville, Kentucky), founded in 1984 by John Schnatter. Revenue is about $2 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (PZZA). Strong consumer brand and a major sports sponsor, including NFL and college partnerships.

Xingsheng Youxuan (Xingsheng Selected) is a Changsha, Hunan based community group-buying platform, where residents order groceries and daily goods via mini-programs, with next-day pickup at neighbourhood community stores. Revenue comes from product sales and fees. Reported to be backed by investors including Alibaba. Crunchbase shows about $5.2 billion in total funding. Private. Regional consumer brand within China's community commerce segment.

about: iFood is Brazil's largest food delivery platform, connecting consumers with restaurants, supermarkets and pharmacies via its app, with its own delivery fleet and payment services. Based in Osasco, Sao Paulo, it was founded in 2011, and is controlled by Prosus after buying out Just Eat Takeaway's stake in 2022. Revenue comes from commissions, delivery fees and advertising. Very strong consumer brand in Brazil with heavy marketing and sports partnerships.

US packaged baked goods brand, makers of Twinkies, Cupcakes, Ding Dongs and Donettes, based in Lenexa, Kansas; it was acquired by J.M. Smucker in 2023 for about $5.6 billion after being listed on Nasdaq. Sells through grocery retailers and convenience stores. Strong US consumer brand recognition. Hostess is part of Smucker's snack portfolio and also owns Voortman cookies, selling in US supermarkets and convenience stores.

Charlotte, North Carolina doughnut maker, founded 1937 in Winston-Salem, selling Original Glazed and other treats through shops, delivery and thousands of grocery points of access in about 40 countries. Revenue is about $1.7 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (DNUT). Very strong consumer brand with global recognition and heavy co-branding and sponsorship marketing. Krispy Kreme has about 14,000 points of access, uses a hub-and-spoke model and operates in the US, UK, Australia and Mexico.

Milan-based Italian spirits company, founded 1860, owning Aperol, Campari, Wild Turkey, Skyy, Grand Marnier and Appleton Estate, sold in about 190 countries with revenue near EUR 3.1 billion. Listed in Milan (CPR). Strong consumer brand, especially in cocktails, with Aperol Spritz a global trend; active in motorsport and sports sponsorship. Campari employs about 5,000 people and has a large presence in Italy, the US, Brazil and Jamaica.

Cbc, the Guatemala-based Central America Beverage Corporation, is a food and beverage company known as a major bottler for PepsiCo products and local brands across Central America and the Caribbean. The input shows a franchising and beverage focus with funding of $875 million. Strong regional consumer reach. CBC distributes beverages and also operates franchise restaurants and other businesses across Central America and the Caribbean.

about: Italian tomato and prepared foods producer, based in Angri, Campania, supplying canned tomato products, beverages and sauces to retailers across Europe, with a large UK trade. B2B and private label with limited consumer recognition. Sells canned tomatoes, pasta sauces, fruit juices and fruit-based drinks for retailers and private label across Europe. Founded 1954. Low consumer recognition. La Doria is among the leading Italian suppliers of canned tomato products to British supermarkets.

Mexican subsidiary of PepsiCo, with bottling and snack brands such as Sabritas, Gamesa and Pepsi, serving the Mexican market. Strong consumer visibility; sponsor of football in Mexico. Part of PepsiCo, with strong distribution to shops across Mexico. The input shows an industrial base in Morelos. Product mix is carbonated drinks and bottled water. Strong consumer awareness across Mexico through retail and corner shops.

Dutch retail group formed by the 2016 merger of Ahold and Delhaize, owning Albert Heijn, Delhaize, Food Lion, Giant and Stop & Shop, with roughly 7,500 stores in Europe and the US and revenue of about EUR 90 billion. Headquartered in Zaandam and listed on Euronext Amsterdam (AD). Very high consumer visibility in its home markets, mostly local brands. Ahold Delhaize serves around 60 million customers weekly and employs roughly 400,000 people, and it sells grocery e-commerce under many local banners.

Beijing-based Chinese dairy producer, founded 1999, selling Mengniu milk, Milk Deluxe, Future Star, yoghurt and Suan Suan Ru products, and ice cream, to consumers across China through retail and e-commerce. Revenue is about CNY 90 billion. Listed in Hong Kong (2319), with state-owned COFCO as the largest shareholder. Household name in China with extensive sports and TV sponsorship, including Olympic partnerships.

Fast-casual Mexican restaurant chain founded in Denver in 1993 and now headquartered in Newport Beach, California, with about 3,900 restaurants mainly in the US plus Canada, the UK, France and Germany. Revenue is about $11 billion and it employs about 130,000 people. Listed on the NYSE (CMG). Very strong US consumer brand, now expanding internationally and sponsoring sport. Chipotle's menu is built around burritos, bowls and tacos, with ingredients it describes as responsibly sourced, and digital orders make up a large share of sales.

Atchison, Kansas-based producer of distilled spirits and specialty wheat proteins, supplying bourbon, whiskey and gin to brand owners and selling its own brands such as Penelope, Rebel and George Remus. Revenue is about $700 million. Listed on Nasdaq (MGPI). Mainly a B2B supplier, with growing consumer whiskey brands. MGP also sells wheat protein and starch ingredients for the food industry. It employs about 700 people in Kansas, Indiana and Kentucky.

Milan-based Italian food group, successor to Newlat Food, making and selling pasta, dairy, bakery and special-diet products, including Polenghi, Centrale del Latte d'Italia and Delverde, across Europe and the UK. Customers are retailers, private-label buyers and food service. Listed on the Milan exchange. Several mid-sized consumer brands with limited international recognition. Nexture owns Italian food brands and has factories in Italy and abroad, and it targets mass retailers and discount supermarkets.

Novus Foods is a Delphos, Ohio-based maker of refrigerated desserts, dips and snacks, supplying retailers and foodservice customers across the US. The input shows a food and beverage focus with $500 million of funding, which may reflect an acquisition or financing. Little consumer brand awareness beyond store labels. Its refrigerated dessert and dip lines are typically sold under retailers' own labels, so the company has little consumer name recognition.

about: Indore-based Indian edible oil and packaged food maker, formerly Ruchi Soya, now controlled by the Patanjali Ayurved group of Baba Ramdev and Acharya Balkrishna. Sells palm and soya oils, food products and Patanjali-branded nutrition goods across India. Listed in India (PATANJALI). Very strong consumer brand in India, with an unusually large retail reach. Patanjali Foods employs a few thousand people, operates refineries and mills, and has a large rural network across India.

Mannheim-based German sugar and food group, Europe's largest sugar producer, with segments in sugar, special products (Freiberger frozen pizza), CropEnergies bioethanol and fruit. Revenue is about EUR 9 billion. Listed in Frankfurt (SZU), majority held by cooperative beet growers. Consumer exposure through food brands, mostly B2B sugar. Sudzucker employs about 19,000 people and sells sugar under brands such as Sudzucker, and also owns Freiberger and Sudzucker's Belgian sugar arm Raffinerie Tirlemontoise.

Smithfield, Virginia-based pork producer and packaged meats company, with brands including Smithfield, Eckrich, Nathan's Famous, Armour and Farmland. Sells to US grocers and foodservice and exports worldwide. Owned by WH Group of Hong Kong until a January 2025 listing on Nasdaq (SFD). Revenue about $15 billion. Strong consumer brand in US supermarkets. Smithfield employs about 35,000 people, operates farms and plants in the US and Europe, and exports pork to Asia and Mexico.

Korean-Japanese conglomerate Lotte Group, with HQ shown in the input as Bothell, Washington (US unit). The group is active in confectionery, retail, hotels, theme parks, chemicals and food, with brands like Lotte chocolates, Lotte Hotels and Lotte World. Strong consumer brand in Korea and Japan, and sports sponsorship in baseball. Lotte's divisions include Lotte Confectionery, Lotte Mart, Lotte Chemical and Lotte Hotel, and the group owns the Lotte Giants baseball team.

Tempe, Arizona-based drive-through coffee chain, Dutch Bros, founded 1992 in Oregon, with over 1,000 shops across the US. Listed on the NYSE (BROS). Revenue about $1.5 billion. Strong regional consumer brand, expanding nationally. The chain has over 1,000 locations, mainly in the western US, and is expanding eastward. Revenue is about $1.5 billion. Dutch Bros also sells energy drinks, teas and smoothies, and draws strong loyalty from regular customers.

Restaurant Brands International is the parent of fast-food chains Burger King, Tim Hortons, Popeyes and Firehouse Subs, plus the Carrefour-licensed Burger King and Tim Hortons international franchising operations. It earns royalties and rent from franchisees across more than 120 countries and over 30,000 restaurants, with system sales above 40 billion dollars. Created in 2014 when Burger King merged with Tim Hortons, backed by 3G Capital and Berkshire Hathaway; headquartered in Toronto and listed on the NYSE and TSX (QSR). Massive global consumer brands that already do large sports and entertainment marketing.

Pet Valu is a Canadian specialty retailer of pet food and supplies, with roughly 800 corporate and franchise stores in Canada under the Pet Valu and Chico banners, plus the Hartz Cats and Dogs selling business and online sales. Customers are pet owners buying premium food, treats and accessories. Founded in 1976 and headquartered in Markham, Ontario; listed on the TSX (PET) since 2021. Revenue is about 1.2 billion Canadian dollars. Well known Canadian consumer brand but with no presence in the other F1 markets.

Coca-Cola Beverages Florida is a Tampa-based bottler and distributor of Coca-Cola products across much of Florida, manufacturing and delivering soft drinks, water, juices and energy drinks to supermarkets, restaurants and convenience stores. It is one of the large regional Coca-Cola bottlers in the United States, operating production plants and distribution depots with thousands of employees. B2B route-to-market business under the globally famous Coca-Cola brand, but little standalone consumer brand awareness.

about: Athletic Brewing is a Connecticut-based producer of non-alcoholic craft beer, with brands such as Run Wild IPA, Upside Dawn and Free Wave Hazy IPA, brewed at facilities in Milford, Connecticut and San Diego. Founded in 2017, it sells through grocery, bars and online, and is the largest non-alcoholic craft brewer in the United States, with sales around 100 million dollars or more. It raised funding of about 300 million dollars from investors including Spectrum Equity. Growing consumer brand with a sports and wellness image.

Mountaintop Beverage is a West Virginia manufacturer based in Morgantown that produces aseptic and extended-shelf-life beverages, including dairy, plant-based and protein drinks, for brand owners under contract. Customers are food and beverage brands and retailers, so it is a B2B co-packer. Reported funding of about 300 million dollars relates to its large production facility build-out. No consumer brand of its own, so little public awareness.

about: Gu Ming (Guming) is a Chinese milk tea chain, established in 2010 in Zhejiang, selling tea drinks with fresh fruit and milk through thousands of franchised stores across China. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (1364) in 2025. Headquartered in Wenling, with revenue largely from franchising and supplying ingredients to its stores. Highly visible in Chinese cities, with small presence outside China.

iD Fresh Food is a Bengaluru-based Indian packaged-food company known for fresh ready-to-cook idli and dosa batter, parathas, chapatis and filter coffee, sold through supermarkets and quick-commerce apps in India, the Middle East and the United States. Founded in 2005 by P.C. Musthafa and cousins, it has a large cold chain and raised about 266 million dollars, with Premji Invest as a major investor. Strong brand among urban Indian households.

Zevia is a Los Angeles beverage company selling zero-calorie, zero-sugar soda sweetened with stevia, in flavours such as Cola, Ginger Root Beer and Orange, plus energy drinks and mixers. Sold in grocery stores and online across the US and Canada, it listed on the NYSE (ZVIA) in 2021. Founded in 2007, with revenue around 160 million dollars. Known niche brand in the health-conscious soft drink market.

San Miguel Corporation is the Philippines' largest conglomerate by sales, founded in 1890 and based in Mandaluyong, with businesses in food and beverage (San Miguel Beer, Ginebra San Miguel, Magnolia), packaging, energy (Meralco stake, power plants), infrastructure (airports, tollways) and fuel retail. Controlled by the Ramon Ang-led group, and listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (SMC). Revenue is around 1.4 trillion pesos. San Miguel Beer is a household brand with heavy sports sponsorship, including basketball.

Cefetra Group is a Rotterdam-based international trader and supplier of food and feed ingredients, including grains, oilseeds, soy and animal feed raw materials, serving feed mills, food producers and farmers across Europe and beyond. It is privately owned. B2B commodity trader with no consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Cefetra is an international food and feed ingredient supplier.

about: Chefs' Warehouse is a US specialty food distributor based in Ridgefield, Connecticut, supplying premium ingredients, proteins, pastry, cheese and imported products to restaurants, hotels, caterers and retailers, mostly in major US metropolitan areas and Canada. Listed on Nasdaq (CHEF), with revenue of about 3.5 billion dollars. Customers are chefs and foodservice operators. B2B distributor with no consumer brand awareness.

SalMar is a Norwegian salmon farmer, one of the world's largest, producing Atlantic and organic salmon from farms along Norway's coast and in Iceland, with its own processing plants. Based in Frøya (Crunchbase shows Kverva), it sells to retailers and food processors in Europe, Asia and the US. Listed on Oslo Bors (SALM), with revenue of about 20 billion Norwegian kroner. Mostly B2B, with limited consumer recognition.

Compass Group is the world's largest contract catering company, headquartered in Chertsey, UK and listed on the London Stock Exchange (CPG). It runs restaurants and food services for businesses, schools, hospitals, sports venues, defence sites and offices across around 30 countries, through brands such as Levy and Eurest, with revenue of about 40 billion pounds and more than 500,000 employees. Levy provides hospitality at major sporting events. B2B brand with low consumer recognition, but strong in event hospitality.

Impossible Foods is a Redwood City, California food company, founded in 2011, that makes plant-based meat products such as the Impossible Burger, sausage and nuggets, using a soy leghemoglobin ingredient. It sells through supermarkets and restaurant chains such as Burger King, and operates in the US, Canada, Asia and Europe. Funding is about $1.9 billion from investors including Khosla and Temasek. Strong consumer brand in plant-based food, and has previously sponsored sport.

Ferrero is an Italian-founded confectionery group, with its holding in Luxembourg and operational base in Alba, Italy and Arlon. It makes Nutella, Kinder, Ferrero Rocher, Tic Tac and Raffaello and acquired Nestle's US candy business and Kellogg's cookies. Revenue is about 18 billion euros, from around 170 countries. Privately held by the Ferrero family. Extremely strong consumer brand, and active in sports sponsorship.

Greencross is Australasia's leading specialist pet care retailer and vet operator, based in Brisbane, with Petbarn, City Farmers and Greencross Vets, and over 400 vet clinics and stores. It sells pet food, supplies and veterinary services to pet owners. It was bought by TPG Capital in 2019 after a public listing, with funding shown at about 1.5 billion Australian dollars. Strong consumer brand in Australia.

Toast is a Boston-based restaurant technology company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TOST), which sells cloud-based point-of-sale systems, payments, payroll, online ordering and delivery tools to over 130,000 restaurant locations, mainly in the US. It earns subscriptions and payment fees, with revenue of about $5 billion. Known among restaurateurs, and has sponsored sports properties such as Boston teams.
